where each assignment folds the corresponding half into the other. In a finite alphabet the maximum exists. Both folded values are at most that maximum; if it is positive the inequality forces both to equal it, and if zero equality is immediate. Thus maximizing assignments remain maximizing under both folds. Starting with a one-cell-wide identical strip, successive boundary folds extend it to a half-period and then the full coordinate. A fold in another coordinate preserves equality along the coordinates already filled, so repeating in each coordinate yields a constant maximizing assignment, without a power-of-two hypothesis. Normalize each chamber function by R(Fc) + ε. Every constant assignment has value at most one, hence the mixed maximum does too. Rescaling and ε ↓0 prove
